questions.q: How many product choices did supermarkets have on average in 2008?
questions.why: Schwartz notes supermarkets rose to over 47,000 items by 2008.

questions.q: What term does Schwartz use for people who settle for "good enough"?
questions.why: He describes satisficers as those who accept good enough choices.

questions.q: How many possible stereo system combos can a single electronics store offer?
questions.why: Schwartz cites a store offering 6.5 million combinations.

questions.q: According to Schwartz, what happens to happiness as options increase?
a: It declines regardless of the choice made
questions.why: He argues more options make people less happy no matter what they pick.

questions.q: What does Schwartz claim is a main cause of modern unhappiness?
questions.why: He links abundant choice to contemporary unhappiness.
